title: R' Abba Sumka
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot, chapter 9, halakhah 1, with Hyman’s additional locator נו., mentions R’ Berechyah and R’ Chelbo speaking in his name. Bamidbar Rabbah 3:7 gives Rabbi Berechyah, son of Rabbi Chelbo, in the name of Abba Samokid. Hyman says it SHOULD READ “Rabbi Berechyah and R’ Chelbo” and “Abba Samokah.” In Tanchuma, Bereshit 6, R’ Berechyah speaks in the name of R’ Abba HaAdmoni. According to the scholar Hyman cites as הרש״ב, of blessed memory, this is R’ Abba Sumka, since samok is Aramaic for red.

notes.text: Hyman proposes changing Berechyah son of Chelbo to Berechyah and Chelbo, and Samokid to Sumka. The commentator siglum RShB remains unidentified here. Red is the semantic connection with Admoni.

The saved whole Torat Emet Bamidbar Rabbah 3:7 scalar has full Rabbi Berechyah BEN full Rabbi Chelbo in Abba Samokid's name. Hyman's SHOULD READ and-Chelbo and Samokah are attributed corrections, not proof these named readings are corrupt. The additional Berakhot locator נו. remains literal: its function is not newly established as daf 56a. The uninspected Tanchuma citation and RShB commentator identification remain unresolved; Shlomo Buber is only a prior unverified lead. Red is the semantic link between sumak and Admoni, not sufficient identity evidence. Full titles are confined to the actual named Bamidbar occurrences; other title components remain R'.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1 names Berechyah and Chelbo together in Abba Sumka’s name. Bamidbar Rabbah 3:7 reads Berechyah son of Chelbo and Abba Samokid. The Abba HaAdmoni passage is Buber’s Bereshit 7:1. In note 41, Buber prefers HaAdmoni to the Rome manuscript’s HaArami and explicitly suggests that he may be Abba Sumka. Buber also considers Abba ben Yamina or Zimna and cites a parallel in Kedoshim without the epithet. The identification is an editorial conjecture.
